name: @dapplelight/signet-mcp

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search every Signet doc section, exported symbol, component and recipe by keywords. Start here when you do not know where something lives. Returns refs to pass to read_doc, get_export, get_component or recipe.

query.description: Keywords, e.g. 'rate limit durable object' or 'parseBody'

tools.name: read_doc
tools.description: Read a Signet doc (a package README, API, CONVENTIONS, CONTRACT, MIGRATION, CHANGELOG...) whole or one section. The same text as the signet://docs/<name> resource, for clients without resource support.

name.description: One of: signet, api, conventions, migration, changelog, contributing, publishing, repo-guide, ai, cli, config, create-signet-app, agents, db, analytics, lib, mcp-agents, mcp, payments-agents, payments, server, spec, test, contract, tokens, ui

section.description: A heading (or its slug) to return just that section, with its subsections

tools.name: list_exports
tools.description: List every import path a Signet package exports, with each path's summary and symbol names. Omit package for all of them. Use get_export for a symbol's signature and doc comment.

tools.name: get_export
tools.description: Get one exported symbol: its declaration signature, doc comment, kind and source file, plus every other import path that exports it.

tools.name: list_components
tools.description: List the @dapplelight/signet-ui components with their import paths and exported names.

tools.name: get_component
tools.description: Get one component: its props (parameter list and Props types from the source), cva variants and defaults, a usage example, and which theme-contract variables its classes read.

tools.name: compose_component
tools.description: Plan a UI piece from Signet behaviours and parts. Give the need in words ("command palette", "collapsible navigation", "progress through steps"); returns the closest signet-ui components with their behaviour recipe, parts, token classes and an example, plus the signet-ui/behaviors hooks and the guide for building something new from them.

need.description: What the UI must do, e.g. 'a searchable command menu'

tools.name: plan_page
tools.description: Plan a whole page from words ("a pricing page with monthly and yearly plans"). Returns the block to add (with its signet add block command), the components it uses, server modules, the matching recipe, the data the page needs and the files to create with a one-line purpose each. No LLM call: the same description gives the same plan.

description.description: What the page is for, e.g. 'a pricing page with monthly and yearly plans'

target.description: web: the page. api: its server side. full: both.

tools.name: list_themes
tools.description: List the shipped themes and how to import one.

tools.name: get_theme
tools.description: Get one theme: import path, description, the theme it extends, and its CSS when include_css is true (copy it to start your own theme).

tools.name: list_tokens
tools.description: List the theme contract's variables (78 required, 16 optional) with their group. A theme is valid when it defines every required one.

tools.name: check_theme
tools.description: Validate a theme's CSS against CONTRACT.md: every required variable defined, optional slots wired in both modes, Tailwind's stock palette untouched, no @source, and WCAG contrast for the text, ring and input pairs (light and dark) as the tokens package's own test checks them. Returns findings with fixes.

tools.name: build_theme
tools.description: Build a whole theme from one brand colour: primary, surfaces, text, borders, status accents, charts, focus (and money on finance), light and dark, derived in OKLCH on top of a shipped base theme. Text tokens are guaranteed WCAG 4.5:1 on their backgrounds; tokens moved to get there are listed in adjustments. format css gives a theme file to import in place of the base; tokens gives W3C Design Tokens JSON; figma gives the Figma Variables API body. Optional per-component density (compact, comfortable, spacious).

tools.name: scaffold_app
tools.description: Get the exact create-signet-app command for a new web app, Worker API or composed starter (saas, launch, api-billing, ...), the files it will create, and the next steps. Use scaffold_files instead if you cannot run a shell.

name.description: Directory and package name, e.g. my-app

template.description: web: Vite + React + Signet UI. api: Hono Worker.

theme.description: Theme for the web template; ignored for api

starter.description: A web app and its API composed from parts, instead of template: full (every part, web + API); blank (no parts: the shell, the API and the database); saas (a paid team product: orgs, admin, billing, inbox, account, privacy); launch (before launch: sign-in, waitlist, invites, referrals, feedback, privacy); internal-tool (for your own team: orgs and roles, the admin panel, approval workflows); api-billing (the API half only: sign-in, API keys, billing webhooks); ai-app (an AI product: spend caps per user, billing, account, privacy); paywall (sell access: plans, entitlements, billing, remote paywalls); automation (durable workflows with approvals, and an inbox to tell people); dashboard (a sidebar shell and an overview: stat tiles, a chart, a table); pwa (installable and offline: web manifest, service worker, install prompt)

tools.name: scaffold_files
tools.description: Return every file create-signet-app would write (path and full contents, package.json included), for an agent that writes files itself. Write them under a new directory named after the app, then run bun install.

name.description: Directory and package name, e.g. my-app

template.description: web: Vite + React + Signet UI. api: Hono Worker.

theme.description: Theme for the web template; ignored for api

tools.name: check_app
tools.description: Check an app against Signet's conventions: no env read at module scope in server modules, rate limiting wired with a trust setting, signet-doctor's Durable Object binding/migration/export checks, CSRF, the error handler, the env schema against wrangler vars, Tailwind @source for the components, and (in the Signet repo) no domain vocabulary in base packages. Pass files (path -> contents, relative to the app root) or a local directory path. Returns findings with fixes.

path.description: App root on this machine, absolute or relative to the server's working directory

tools.name: recipe
tools.description: Step-by-step, code-included recipe for a common job, assembled from the Signet docs: what to install, the doc sections in order, and how to verify. Tasks: add-auth, add-rate-limit, add-csrf, add-error-envelope, add-env, add-api-client, add-web-push, add-ai-extraction, add-ai-chat, payments, add-growth, add-realtime, add-workflows, add-collab, add-data-editing, add-india, add-analytics, add-portability-adapters, add-jobs, add-uploads, add-db, publish-an-api, add-plans, add-monetisation, add-abuse-protection, add-experiments, add-subscription-charts, add-funnels, add-mcp-tools, mcp-by-default, add-oauth, add-logging, add-component-source, add-tests, add-backend-module, add-theme. Free text works too.

task.description: A recipe id or a description, e.g. 'add rate limit'

tools.name: migration
tools.description: What changed between two versions, from CHANGELOG.md (with the breaking and migration bullets pulled out) plus any 'Migrating from' section in the package's README. Gives current versions too.

from.description: The version you are on, e.g. 0.3.0

to.description: Target version, or 'unreleased' for everything after from

package.description: e.g. server; omit for every package

instructions:
Signet is a TypeScript kit for web apps and their APIs: token-driven React components, CSS-variable themes, a Hono/Workers server kit, a client lib and structured AI calls. These tools answer from the Signet repo itself, indexed when this server was built.

Start with search_docs when unsure. Before writing an import, confirm it with get_export. New app: scaffold_app (or scaffold_files without a shell). A feature: recipe. UI: list_components, get_component, compose_component for a need described in words. A whole page from words: plan_page. Themes: list_themes, get_theme, check_theme, build_theme (from a brand colour). Before finishing: check_app. Upgrading: migration. Docs are resources at signet://docs/<name> and through read_doc.
